pathway.title: MGM Resorts International — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is improving because debt fell, not because earnings grew. Total leverage is 2.54x against 2.57x at year-end, but adjusted EBITDA was 20.37% lower in Q3 2026 than a year earlier, between 8.04% and 10.74% lower after removing Northfield Park and prior-year insurance proceeds, and 8.12% lower over the last twelve months, so the lower ratios depend on debt reduction holding while earnings stabilise. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31

Rent makes the earnings base more fragile than headline leverage suggests. Fixed-charge cover that adds rent to both sides fell to 1.69x from 1.77x, rent absorbs 51.11% of adjusted EBITDA before rent, and Las Vegas Strip Segment Adjusted EBITDAR fell 11.66% on 1.53% lower revenue because rent and payroll do not flex. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C3; calculation C10

Liquidity is the main strength and holds up under the sensitivities tested. Cash and the undrawn parent revolver cover the 2027 and 2028 maturities 2.15x, or 2.86x for the parent alone, and nothing matures before 2027; if adjusted EBITDA fell a further 10%, net leverage would be 1.63x rather than 1.47x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C4; calculation C7

Diversification helps, but Las Vegas pricing and Macau hold drive the earnings. Las Vegas Strip Resorts gives 48.06% of revenue and 57.07% of segment EBITDAR and MGM China 25.62% and 22.49%, while MGM Digital still loses money; the average Las Vegas room rate fell 8% in Q3 2026 with flat occupancy, and Macau revenue grew on a higher win percentage while the main floor drop fell 10%. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C8; calculation C11

Cash priorities compete, and management restraint is what protects creditors. Buybacks took 84.10% of operating cash flow after capital expenditure in FY2025 but 25.21% in the nine months of 2026, and the remaining MGM Osaka funding is about 2.02x that nine-month free cash flow; if all of it were added to net debt with no cash generation, net leverage would reach 2.41x. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C6; calculation C7

Structure and contingent claims thin the cushion. MGM China holds 40.89% of principal debt outside the parent's guarantee group and shares each dividend with other holders, the Bellagio shortfall guarantee is USD 3.01 billion with a second USD 3.0 billion guarantee unresolved, and lease covenants can require collateral of 6 months to 2 years of rent. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C11

Shareholder and governance risk is Medium, not low. The voting agreement of 2026-04-03 with IAC Inc. and Barry Diller was amended on 2026-10-28 and its terms are not supplied, no exchange offer, priming or drop-down is described, and the only covenant relief found is a 2023 waiver at MGM China that expired after 2024. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mgm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2024-12-31_mgm-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 123

cells.text: Delaware holding company that, through subsidiaries, runs casino resorts with hotels, convention space, dining, entertainment and retail, plus online gaming and sports betting; revenue is mostly cash-based and results are not seasonal
Four: Las Vegas Strip Resorts, Regional Operations, MGM China and MGM Digital; corporate operations and the unconsolidated ventures sit in Corporate and other

Nine resorts; nine months to 2026-09-30 revenue USD 6,304.815 million (48.06% of consolidated revenue) and Segment Adjusted EBITDAR USD 2,015.106 million (57.07% of the segment total); over half of its revenue is typically non-gaming

Six domestic casinos at 2026-09-30 after the April 2026 sale of MGM Northfield Park; revenue USD 2,725.212 million (20.78%) and Segment Adjusted EBITDAR USD 782.275 million (22.16%); the majority of its revenue is typically gaming

About 56% owned and consolidated; MGM Macau and MGM Cotai operate under a concession to 2032-12-31; revenue USD 3,361.083 million (25.62%), Segment Adjusted EBITDAR USD 794.161 million (22.49%); gaming taxes of USD 1,501.762 million took 44.68% of segment revenue

LeoVegas and other consolidated online gaming subsidiaries, headquartered in Sweden and Malta; revenue USD 562.715 million (4.29%) with a Segment Adjusted EBITDAR loss of USD 60.695 million (USD 83.339 million a year earlier); operations in Brazil stopped in September 2026

50% of BetMGM North America Venture, jointly controlled with Entain plc and accounted for under the equity method; about 40% of MGM Osaka Corporation at 2026-09-30, developing an integrated resort in Osaka, Japan

Leases the real estate of its domestic properties under triple net leases that require it to pay substantially all property costs and to spend a set share of revenue on capital expenditure; annual contractual cash rent over the next twelve months is USD 1.8 billion
United States USD 12,411.625 million (70.77%); China USD 4,464.095 million (25.45%); other USD 661.963 million (3.77%)

Premium and leisure gaming customers, conventions and groups, and online players; volume at the properties drives the price of rooms and amenities, and the MGM Rewards loyalty programme links gaming and non-gaming spend

About 44,000 full-time and 18,000 part-time employees in the United States and 16,000 internationally at 2025-12-31; about 37,000 US employees are under collective bargaining agreements, some of which expire in 2026

runs.text: Strength 1, liquidity and a clear maturity runway. Cash of USD 2,395.957 million (of which about USD 598 million sits in MGM China) and an undrawn USD 2,275.000 million parent revolver cover principal due in 2027 and 2028 2.15x, with nothing due before 2027. Liquidity therefore removes near-term refinancing and cash-shortfall risk and gives management time to rebuild earnings. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C4

Strength 2, conduct that is consistent with creditor interests so far. Maturities were repaid or refinanced on schedule, debt at carrying value fell by USD 561.155 million in nine months, the revolver is undrawn and covenant compliance is stated for all three facilities, which lowers the chance of value transfer and supports market access. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

Strength 3, scale and diversification across four segments. Revenue of USD 17,537.683 million in FY2025 came from Las Vegas, regional casinos, Macau and online gaming, so a weak quarter in one segment is partly absorbed; regional same-store revenue rose 1% in Q3 2026 and Macau reached a record 17.1% market share. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

Strength 4, asset-light flexibility and asset sales. Selling leased casinos removes rent as well as earnings (USD 53 million of annual rent for Northfield Park), and Springfield for USD 443 million offers further optionality, so management can reshape fixed charges. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

Strength 5, falling capital intensity. Capital expenditure was 20.04% lower in the nine months of 2026 and operating cash flow after capital expenditure of USD 1,041.360 million funded buybacks, distributions and MGM Osaka with cash left for debt repayment. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C5; calculation C13

Weakness 1, earnings falling against fixed rent. Adjusted EBITDA was 20.37% lower in Q3 2026 (between 8.04% and 10.74% lower like for like) and fixed-charge cover fell to 1.69x, because annual rent of USD 1.8 billion and payroll do not flex with revenue, so a further decline in room rates or hold would cut cover quickly. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C14

Weakness 2, large commitments outside debt. Remaining MGM Osaka funding of about USD 2.1 billion, a 50% guarantee against a 40% interest, lease collateral covenants and landlord guarantees of USD 3.01 billion (with a possible second USD 3.0 billion) are claims on cash and balance sheet that do not appear in debt at carrying value. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30

Weakness 3, Macau structure and concession. MGM China holds 40.89% of principal debt outside the parent's guarantee group, its concession expires on 2032-12-31 and growth rested on a higher win percentage while volume fell, so parent creditors depend on subsidiary dividends shared with other holders. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C8; calculation C11

Weakness 4, discretionary shareholder returns with an unreadable voting agreement. USD 1.4 billion of repurchase authorisation remains and management links the amended voting agreement to repurchases, so leverage depends on a policy choice, not a documented limit. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mgm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41

Weakness 5, a loss-making digital segment and concentrated high-end exposure. MGM Digital lost USD 60.695 million at segment EBITDAR in nine months and left Brazil in September 2026, and a significant part of operating income comes from high-end gaming customers whose share is not measured. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Two disposals of leased casinos are under way. MGM Northfield Park was sold in April 2026 for USD 546 million in cash, USD 540 million net of adjustments and costs, and the master lease was amended to remove it and cut annual cash rent by USD 53 million; MGM Springfield is agreed for USD 443 million, subject to approvals and termination rights, with no closing date or net proceeds stated. Management links the Northfield Park proceeds to a strong balance sheet and to share repurchases. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-04-29_mgmex991q12026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, page 1

No new parent notes were issued in 2026. The only new bond is MGM China's USD 750 million of 6.25% notes due 2033, issued in May 2026 as USD 750 million of 5.875% notes matured, and the parent repaid its USD 400 million 4.625% notes due 2026 in September from cash. The newest parent borrowing is the senior secured yen facility, entered in October 2025 as a JPY45.2 billion term loan and raised to JPY54.2 billion in November 2025; it is secured by a pledge of equity in certain domestic operating properties and is expected to fund part of the MGM Osaka commitment. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

The VICI master lease was amended and restated in April 2026 to remove Northfield Park, which lowered annual cash rent to USD 722 million before the 2% escalator raised it to USD 736 million for the lease year from 2026-05-01. The lease has a 25-year initial term from 2022-04-29 and three renewal options of ten years, and the other four leases add about USD 1.0 billion of annual cash rent. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 120–121; calculation C6

Shareholder-facing transactions continue: repurchases run under the USD 2.0 billion plan authorised in April 2025 with USD 1.4 billion remaining, and a voting agreement with IAC Inc. and Barry Diller dated 2026-04-03 was amended and announced on 2026-10-28, with terms not supplied. MGM Osaka funding also continues: JPY23.9 billion was funded in the nine months to 2026-09-30 and JPY19.4 billion in October 2026, after quarter end, with JPY333.0 billion left to fund through 2028. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mgm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MGM Resorts International (issuer mgm-789570), financial foundation as of 2026-11-18 for the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt at carrying value, net debt, leverage, cover, liquidity and maturities from the eight supplied filings and releases, on the consolidated perimeter, current period Q3 2026 against FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage fell to 1.47x adjusted EBITDA at 2026-09-30 from 1.72x at year-end, helped by asset-sale proceeds and free cash flow, while adjusted EBITDA over the last twelve months is below FY2025 and reported EBITDA is flattered by a one-off gain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 94–96; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors should read the improvement as balance-sheet repair rather than earnings growth: cash interest cover on adjusted EBITDA slipped to 5.82x from 6.23x, and the cushion is cash and an undrawn parent revolver, with nothing maturing before 2027. Lease obligations, rent and the MGM Osaka commitment sit outside Total Debt, and MGM China debt and cash sit in a subsidiary owned about 56% by MGM.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C7; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt fell by USD 894.118 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30, to USD 3,273.029 million, because gross debt at carrying value fell by USD 561.155 million after the parent repaid USD 400 million of notes at maturity with cash, MGM China cut its revolving borrowings by USD 156.876 million and refinanced its USD 750 million of maturing notes with new 2033 notes, and the Northfield Park sale brought in USD 513.462 million, while cash rose by USD 332.963 million. Net leverage on last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA is 1.47x, down from 1.72x, and total leverage is 2.54x against 2.57x. The denominator moved the other way: adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months is USD 2,228.592 million against USD 2,425.623 million for FY2025, a change of -8.12%, so the lower ratios depend on the debt reduction holding while earnings stabilise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA, the method's primary denominator, gives 1.39x net and 2.41x total leverage at 2026-09-30, lower than the adjusted ratios of 1.47x and 2.54x. The reason is that reported EBITDA, operating income plus depreciation and amortization, includes a net gain on property transactions of USD 256.229 million over the twelve months (mainly the gain on the Northfield Park sale and on the partial termination of the VICI lease) and is reduced by a goodwill impairment of USD 133.813 million, while the issuer's adjusted measure removes both. Creditors should use the adjusted ratios for the trend and treat the reported ratios as the stated primary basis, not as evidence of stronger earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover on adjusted EBITDA is 5.82x for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, against 6.23x for FY2025 and 5.93x for FY2024, because cash interest paid is little changed (USD 382.798 million for the twelve months against USD 389.128 million) while adjusted EBITDA is lower. On reported EBITDA cover rose to 6.14x from 5.19x for the reasons given above. Adjusted EBITDA is struck after triple net lease rent expense of USD 1,665.718 million in the nine months of 2026, so cover is already a rent-burdened measure; the interest-paid figure is consolidated and includes MGM China.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C7; calculation C4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 1,659.066 million in the nine months of 2026 against USD 1,874.383 million a year earlier, a change of -11.49%, while capital expenditure fell to USD 617.706 million from USD 772.472 million, so operating cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 1,041.360 million against USD 1,101.911 million. That cash went to USD 262.499 million of share repurchases, USD 138.866 million of distributions to noncontrolling owners and USD 154.917 million of investment in unconsolidated affiliates, mainly MGM Osaka; the sale proceeds of USD 513.462 million and the retained balance paid down debt. Buybacks are the discretionary item to watch, because they compete with deleveraging while adjusted EBITDA is falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash of USD 2,395.957 million, of which MGM China held USD 598 million, and USD 2,275.000 million undrawn on the parent revolving facility after USD 25 million of letters of credit compare with no debt maturing before 2027, USD 1,425.000 million maturing in 2027 and USD 750.000 million in 2028. Against that the issuer expects cash interest of USD 315 million to USD 335 million over the next twelve months, annual cash rent of USD 1.8 billion, remaining 2026 capital expenditure of USD 360 million to USD 410 million and about USD 2.1 billion still to fund for MGM Osaka through 2028, part of which it expects to finance with the yen facility. Liquidity covers the maturities comfortably, but fixed claims are large, MGM China cash is held in a 56%-owned subsidiary and reaches the parent through dividends, and the undrawn MGM China facility is not counted because its USD amount is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four risks bear on how the figures should be used. Reported and adjusted EBITDA differ by the one-off items above, and neither is a covenant measure because the credit agreements are not in the set. Balance-sheet cash differs from the cash-flow closing balance by MGM China's restricted cash. The printed net change in cash includes a held-for-sale cash line, so the fixed Net Cash Change row is withheld where it applies. Debt at carrying value omits operating lease liabilities of USD 23.9 billion and finance lease liabilities, which the issuer presents on their own lines, so lease-burdened leverage is far higher than the ratios shown and is not calculated here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: One event after the balance-sheet date changes net debt: the October 2026 funding of JPY19.4 billion, about USD 123 million, of the MGM Osaka commitment, which would lift net debt to USD 3,396.029 million and net leverage to 1.45x on reported EBITDA; the day is not stated. The agreement to sell MGM Springfield for USD 443 million is described as subject to approvals and other conditions, with no closing date, so no pro forma effect is stated. The Northfield Park sale is one economic event with several figures: a gross price of USD 546 million, net consideration of USD 541 million in the second-quarter report and USD 540 million in the third-quarter report, a gain of USD 255 million and then USD 253 million, and cash proceeds of USD 513.462 million in the cash flow statement, which is close to the net consideration less the USD 26 million of cash derecognized with the business although the filings give no reconciliation; the later report's figures are used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer-funded contract liabilities, which carry no interest, were USD 1,244.996 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 1,280.725 million at 2025-12-31, led by customer advances and other (USD 851.424 million), which include casino front money and advance deposits. They are credit-relevant working-capital float rather than ordinary payables: they fund operations while guests hold deposits, chips and loyalty credits, and they can reverse quickly if play or confidence weakens, which would draw on cash that net debt already nets off. The float is about 0.38x net debt, a size that deserves monitoring even though it fell slightly in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MGM Resorts International (issuer mgm-789570), business, transaction and governance review as of 2026-11-18 for the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: operating model, ownership and control, group and debt structure, transactions, shareholder behaviour and governance from the eight supplied filings and releases, current period Q3 2026. Leverage, liquidity and covenant analysis are left to other modules.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MGM is an asset-light casino operator in which the filings identify no controlling sponsor, so creditor risk comes mainly from shareholder returns, leased real estate and joint-venture commitments, and governance risk is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buybacks took 84.10% of operating cash flow after capital expenditure in FY2025 but 25.21% in the nine months of 2026, and management says the amended voting agreement with IAC Inc. and Barry Diller, whose terms are not supplied, supports share repurchases. Rent of USD 1.8 billion a year, about USD 2.1 billion still to fund for MGM Osaka and landlord guarantees draw on the same cash, while the Macau subsidiary holds 40.89% of principal debt outside the parent's guarantee group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C3; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash returned to shareholders is the main policy risk, and it has slowed. Repurchases took 112.05% of operating cash flow after capital expenditure in FY2024 and 84.10% in FY2025, against 25.21% in the nine months of 2026, and USD 1.4 billion of authorisation remains. The common dividend has been suspended since 2023, so buybacks are the discretionary lever that could stop leverage falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The governance that matters most is a shareholder arrangement that cannot be read. The voting agreement of 2026-04-03 with IAC Inc. and Barry Diller was amended on 2026-10-28; neither its terms nor the holders' percentages are in the supplied documents, so control, takeover risk and buyback capacity cannot be measured, and no sponsor, fund life or exit pressure is inferred.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Macau subsidiary holds a large part of the group's debt, cash and earnings outside the parent's guarantee group. MGM China produced 25.62% of nine-month revenue, holds 40.89% of principal debt and USD 598 million of cash, is about 56% owned and shares each dividend with other holders, about 44% of it. A new branding fee moves earnings from it to the parent, its financial covenants were waived through 2024-12-31 after a 2023 amendment, and its concession expires on 2032-12-31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2024-12-31_mgm-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 123; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fixed and contingent claims sit outside reported debt. Rent is USD 1.8 billion a year with lease covenants that require collateral of 6 months to 2 years of rent, MGM Osaka needs about USD 2.1 billion through 2028 with a guarantee for 50% of obligations against a 40% interest, and the Bellagio shortfall guarantee of USD 3.01 billion may be joined by a second USD 3.0 billion guarantee that the notes do not describe.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C8; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pruning the portfolio lowers rent but also earnings, and the use of proceeds is not settled. Northfield Park was sold for USD 546 million with USD 53 million less annual rent, Springfield is agreed for USD 443 million with no closing date, and management links the Northfield Park proceeds to repurchases; Springfield first appears in the third-quarter report although its agreement is dated March 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are sensitive to price and hold, not only volume. On the Las Vegas Strip the average room rate fell 8% with flat occupancy and segment EBITDAR fell 11.66% on 1.53% lower revenue; in Macau revenue grew on a higher win percentage while the drop fell 10%, and gaming taxes take 44.68% of segment revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C4; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting is adequate for monitoring but contingent claims are hard to see. Annual statements are audited with effective internal control and each quarterly report is dated the same day as its earnings release, yet the proxy statement and agreements are not supplied and the annual report's risk factor and commitments note describe the landlord guarantees differently.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a lower risk level is conduct. No exchange offer, priming or drop-down is described, the only covenant relief found is a 2023 waiver at MGM China that expired after 2024, maturities were repaid or refinanced on schedule, covenant compliance is stated for all three credit facilities, the parent revolver is undrawn, debt at carrying value fell over the nine months and buybacks slowed to 25.21% of free cash flow. The strongest evidence for a higher level is what cannot be seen: the voting agreement, the credit agreements and a possible second landlord guarantee of USD 3.0 billion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2024-12-31_mgm-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C5; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to High if buybacks returned above free cash flow, if the amended voting agreement raised repurchase capacity or entrenched a holder, if the second guarantee were confirmed or MGM Osaka costs rose, or if the Springfield proceeds were returned to shareholders rather than used to reduce debt. It would move to Low if the agreement capped a holder's stake without enabling larger buybacks, the guarantees were confirmed at USD 3.01 billion, and the buyback pace stayed near the 2026 level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The voting agreement, its amendment, the holders' percentages and the proxy statement are not supplied, so the Medium level could rise to High if they entrench a holder or raise buyback capacity, or fall to Low if they cap a stake without enabling larger buybacks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit agreement, indenture or lease agreement is supplied, so restricted-payment capacity, guarantor release and landlord collateral triggers are not established, and the conclusion that buybacks are a policy choice rather than a documented constraint cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The annual reports describe two landlord shortfall guarantees while the commitments notes describe one, so contingent claims outside debt may be about double what the notes show and the governance level could rise to High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Springfield's closing date and proceeds, and the use of the Northfield Park proceeds, are not stated, so the finding that disposals lower rent and earnings together cannot be turned into a net effect on debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - MGM Osaka's total cost, the other investors' funding and the guarantee share after the ownership changes are not supplied, so the contingent claim above the 40% interest is not sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The latest document is dated 2026-10-28, so any buyback, financing or disposal after that date could change the level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, MGM presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is a buyback programme that took most of free cash flow in FY2025 and slowed in 2026, which matters because it competes with debt reduction, MGM Osaka funding and rent, and implies that leverage depends on a policy choice rather than a documented limit. Countervailing evidence is the record of on-schedule repayments and refinancings, an undrawn parent revolver, a suspended dividend and clean audit opinions. Further analysis requires the voting agreement, the credit agreements, the proxy statement and a reconciliation of the landlord guarantees.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance review completed with limitations. Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. Key gaps: voting agreement terms, credit agreements, proxy statement, landlord guarantee reconciliation and the use of disposal proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two disposals of leased casinos are under way. MGM Northfield Park was sold in April 2026 for USD 546 million in cash, USD 540 million net of adjustments and costs, and the master lease was amended to remove it and cut annual cash rent by USD 53 million; MGM Springfield is agreed for USD 443 million, subject to approvals and termination rights, with no closing date or net proceeds stated. Management links the Northfield Park proceeds to a strong balance sheet and to share repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new parent notes were issued in 2026. The only new bond is MGM China's USD 750 million of 6.25% notes due 2033, issued in May 2026 as USD 750 million of 5.875% notes matured, and the parent repaid its USD 400 million 4.625% notes due 2026 in September from cash. The newest parent borrowing is the senior secured yen facility, entered in October 2025 as a JPY45.2 billion term loan and raised to JPY54.2 billion in November 2025; it is secured by a pledge of equity in certain domestic operating properties and is expected to fund part of the MGM Osaka commitment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The VICI master lease was amended and restated in April 2026 to remove Northfield Park, which lowered annual cash rent to USD 722 million before the 2% escalator raised it to USD 736 million for the lease year from 2026-05-01. The lease has a 25-year initial term from 2022-04-29 and three renewal options of ten years, and the other four leases add about USD 1.0 billion of annual cash rent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder-facing transactions continue: repurchases run under the USD 2.0 billion plan authorised in April 2025 with USD 1.4 billion remaining, and a voting agreement with IAC Inc. and Barry Diller dated 2026-04-03 was amended and announced on 2026-10-28, with terms not supplied. MGM Osaka funding also continues: JPY23.9 billion was funded in the nine months to 2026-09-30 and JPY19.4 billion in October 2026, after quarter end, with JPY333.0 billion left to fund through 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mgm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by buyback pace relative to free cash flow, an unreadable voting agreement and contingent landlord and joint-venture guarantees, because they can pull cash and claims ahead of creditors, which implies a higher refinancing and liquidity sensitivity if buybacks resume. Countervailing evidence is the on-schedule repayment record, covenant compliance statements and the undrawn parent revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gate tests: issuer identity is supported by the annual report; no sponsor owner is identified, and the only named holder arrangement is the voting agreement whose terms are not supplied; behaviours are issuer-specific, dated and, for repurchases and disposals, show funding; legal capacity (credit agreements) and willingness (documented actions) are kept apart; unsupported facts are written as not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each calculation is listed with its inputs. Amounts are in USD millions unless a row says otherwise and ratios are percentages rounded to two decimals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: the voting agreement of 2026-04-03 and its 2026-10-28 amendment are not supplied, and no holder percentage is stated, so control, takeover risk and buyback capacity are not established; the action is to obtain the agreement, the current report that announced it and the proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: no credit agreement, indenture, lease agreement or compliance certificate is supplied, so covenant levels, restricted-payment capacity, guarantor release and landlord collateral triggers are not established; the action is to obtain the executed documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: the annual reports' risk factor describes a USD 3.0 billion shortfall guarantee for the landlord of Mandalay Bay and MGM Grand Las Vegas that the commitments notes do not describe; the action is to reconcile it with the company or the landlord's financing documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: the closing date, net proceeds and use of proceeds of the Springfield sale, and the use of the Northfield Park proceeds, are not stated; the action is to read the next quarterly report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: the proxy statement, which carries director independence, committees, executive pay and related-party approvals, is incorporated by reference and not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: the total cost of MGM Osaka, the other investors' funding and whether the 50% guarantee share changes as ownership moves toward about 43.5% are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: the terms of the new branding agreement between MGM China and the parent, and the rank and covenants of MGM China's debt, are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: property-level revenue and customer concentration are described but not measured, and no ratings or market prices are supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: events after 2026-10-28 are not covered because no later filing is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MGM Resorts International (issuer mgm-789570), fundamental credit view as of 2026-11-18 for the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business risk, earnings and cash-flow durability, liquidity, leverage, refinancing, structure and shareholder policy, synthesised from the eight supplied filings and releases and the earlier modules' findings, current period Q3 2026. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or position sizing is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MGM's fundamental credit profile is adequate and its leverage is falling, but earnings are softening against fixed rent, so creditors are protected mainly by liquidity and by management restraint on buybacks and MGM Osaka funding rather than by earnings growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage fell to 1.47x adjusted EBITDA at 2026-09-30 from 1.72x at year-end; it is 1.39x on reported EBITDA, or 1.45x on reported EBITDA pro forma for the October 2026 MGM Osaka funding of about USD 123 million, and a pro forma figure on adjusted EBITDA is not established. Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months is 8.12% lower than in FY2025, partly because Northfield Park was sold and prior-year insurance proceeds ended, and rent-burdened fixed-charge cover slipped to 1.69x from 1.77x. Cash and the undrawn revolver cover the 2027 and 2028 maturities 2.15x, so the primary downside is weaker Las Vegas pricing or Macau hold meeting USD 1.8 billion of annual rent and about USD 2.1 billion of MGM Osaka funding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is improving because debt fell, not because earnings grew. Total leverage is 2.54x against 2.57x at year-end, but adjusted EBITDA was 20.37% lower in Q3 2026 than a year earlier, between 8.04% and 10.74% lower after removing Northfield Park and prior-year insurance proceeds, and 8.12% lower over the last twelve months, so the lower ratios depend on debt reduction holding while earnings stabilise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rent makes the earnings base more fragile than headline leverage suggests. Fixed-charge cover that adds rent to both sides fell to 1.69x from 1.77x, rent absorbs 51.11% of adjusted EBITDA before rent, and Las Vegas Strip Segment Adjusted EBITDAR fell 11.66% on 1.53% lower revenue because rent and payroll do not flex.

fields.value: Liquidity is the main strength and holds up under the sensitivities tested. Cash and the undrawn parent revolver cover the 2027 and 2028 maturities 2.15x, or 2.86x for the parent alone, and nothing matures before 2027; if adjusted EBITDA fell a further 10%, net leverage would be 1.63x rather than 1.47x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Diversification helps, but Las Vegas pricing and Macau hold drive the earnings. Las Vegas Strip Resorts gives 48.06% of revenue and 57.07% of segment EBITDAR and MGM China 25.62% and 22.49%, while MGM Digital still loses money; the average Las Vegas room rate fell 8% in Q3 2026 with flat occupancy, and Macau revenue grew on a higher win percentage while the main floor drop fell 10%.

fields.value: Cash priorities compete, and management restraint is what protects creditors. fields.value: Structure and contingent claims thin the cushion. MGM China holds 40.89% of principal debt outside the parent's guarantee group and shares each dividend with other holders, the Bellagio shortfall guarantee is USD 3.01 billion with a second USD 3.0 billion guarantee unresolved, and lease covenants can require collateral of 6 months to 2 years of rent.

fields.value: The strongest evidence for a stronger view is balance-sheet repair and liquidity: net leverage is down to 1.47x, cash and the undrawn revolver cover the 2027 and 2028 maturities 2.15x, nine-month operating cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 1,041.36 million, and management says October trading has rebounded and said in April 2026 that convention bookings were solid. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that earnings, not debt, are moving the wrong way: Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA was 20.37% lower (between 8.04% and 10.74% lower like for like), fixed-charge cover is 1.69x, and the lease, MGM Osaka and guarantee claims all rank ahead of any recovery in equity returns.

fields.value: Strength 1, liquidity and a clear maturity runway. Cash of USD 2,395.957 million (of which about USD 598 million sits in MGM China) and an undrawn USD 2,275.000 million parent revolver cover principal due in 2027 and 2028 2.15x, with nothing due before 2027. Liquidity therefore removes near-term refinancing and cash-shortfall risk and gives management time to rebuild earnings.

fields.value: Strength 2, conduct that is consistent with creditor interests so far. Maturities were repaid or refinanced on schedule, debt at carrying value fell by USD 561.155 million in nine months, the revolver is undrawn and covenant compliance is stated for all three facilities, which lowers the chance of value transfer and supports market access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength 3, scale and diversification across four segments. Revenue of USD 17,537.683 million in FY2025 came from Las Vegas, regional casinos, Macau and online gaming, so a weak quarter in one segment is partly absorbed; regional same-store revenue rose 1% in Q3 2026 and Macau reached a record 17.1% market share.

fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

fields.value: Strength 4, asset-light flexibility and asset sales. Selling leased casinos removes rent as well as earnings (USD 53 million of annual rent for Northfield Park), and Springfield for USD 443 million offers further optionality, so management can reshape fixed charges.

fields.value: Strength 5, falling capital intensity. Capital expenditure was 20.04% lower in the nine months of 2026 and operating cash flow after capital expenditure of USD 1,041.360 million funded buybacks, distributions and MGM Osaka with cash left for debt repayment.

Adjusted EBITDA was 20.37% lower in Q3 2026 (between 8.04% and 10.74% lower like for like) and fixed-charge cover fell to 1.69x, because annual rent of USD 1.8 billion and payroll do not flex with revenue, so a further decline in room rates or hold would cut cover quickly.

fields.value: Weakness 2, large commitments outside debt. Remaining MGM Osaka funding of about USD 2.1 billion, a 50% guarantee against a 40% interest, lease collateral covenants and landlord guarantees of USD 3.01 billion (with a possible second USD 3.0 billion) are claims on cash and balance sheet that do not appear in debt at carrying value.

fields.value: Weakness 3, Macau structure and concession. MGM China holds 40.89% of principal debt outside the parent's guarantee group, its concession expires on 2032-12-31 and growth rested on a higher win percentage while volume fell, so parent creditors depend on subsidiary dividends shared with other holders.

fields.value: Weakness 4, discretionary shareholder returns with an unreadable voting agreement. USD 1.4 billion of repurchase authorisation remains and management links the amended voting agreement to repurchases, so leverage depends on a policy choice, not a documented limit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mgm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness 5, a loss-making digital segment and concentrated high-end exposure. MGM Digital lost USD 60.695 million at segment EBITDAR in nine months and left Brazil in September 2026, and a significant part of operating income comes from high-end gaming customers whose share is not measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MGM is a Delaware holding company whose subsidiaries run nine Las Vegas Strip resorts, six regional casinos, two casino resorts in Macau through its 56%-owned MGM China and an online gaming business, and it holds 50% of BetMGM and about 40% of MGM Osaka. Because it leases the real estate of its domestic properties, the cash that supports debt is earned after rent of USD 1.8 billion a year. Revenue is mostly cash-based and not seasonal, which gives steady daily cash generation, but quarterly results move with hotel rates, hold percentages and conventions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MGM is a publicly traded company with no controlling holder identified in the supplied reports; IAC Inc. and Barry Diller are parties to a voting agreement whose terms are not supplied. Parent notes are guaranteed by the wholly owned material domestic subsidiaries, while MGM China, which carries 40.89% of principal debt and USD 598 million of cash, three domestic casinos, the BetMGM holder and the LeoVegas holder are not guarantors. Noteholders therefore rank behind subsidiary creditors on non-guarantor assets, and the parent reaches MGM China cash only through dividends that other holders share. Business and governance risk is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mgm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is discretionary, cyclical and sensitive to price and hold. In Las Vegas the average room rate fell 8% in Q3 2026 with occupancy flat at 89%, so pricing power is limited, while casino revenue rose 8% on a table win percentage of 25.3% against 22.6%. In Macau revenue rose 5% although the main floor drop fell 10%, and online revenue grew 20.77% in nine months. The result is that revenue visibility is short, and cash flow depends on rates and hold that the issuer says it does not fully control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are thin against fixed costs. Las Vegas Strip payroll rose 3.42% in nine months while revenue rose 0.47%, the Q3 2026 segment EBITDAR margin fell to 27.16% from 30.28%, gaming taxes take 44.68% of Macau revenue and 19.36% of regional revenue, and annual rent of USD 1.8 billion is fixed with 2% escalators. Margins can be defended only with price or volume, because cost flexibility is limited by rent, union contracts covering about 37,000 US employees (some expire in 2026) and lease minimum capital expenditure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 120–121; calculation C10; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is solid but fully allocated. Nine-month operating cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 1,041.360 million against USD 1,101.911 million, a 5.50% fall, and it funded buybacks of USD 262.499 million, distributions to noncontrolling holders of USD 138.866 million and MGM Osaka funding of USD 154.917 million, with the Northfield Park proceeds of USD 513.462 million and the remainder repaying net debt. Capital expenditure fell 20.04% and USD 360 million to USD 410 million is planned for the rest of 2026, but leases set minimum spending, so capital expenditure is only partly flexible.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C5; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is high and new capacity is arriving: Las Vegas has many casino hotels and competitors have expanded or plan to expand rooms and convention space, and MGM China competes with five other concessionaires, so rate and share pressure feeds directly into EBITDAR. Entry barriers are high because gaming licences and Macau concessions are limited, which protects existing cash flow. Substitutes matter: iGaming and online sports betting can reduce visits and spend at the properties, which is a long-run risk to land-based revenue. Buyer power is moderate: leisure customers are price sensitive, as the 8% fall in the Las Vegas room rate shows, and premium players are offered high-limit rooms and lounges. Supplier power is concentrated in labour, with about 37,000 US employees under union agreements, and in landlords, whose rent is fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory and economic factors are credit drivers here. The Macau concession expires on 2032-12-31 and gaming-law and cross-border travel changes can reduce visitation; a temporary government ban on fixed-odds betting and online casino games stopped operations in Brazil in September 2026; and trade tension and tariffs could cut cross-border travel. Social and technological factors matter mainly through online competition. Yen and Hong Kong dollar exposures arise from MGM Osaka funding and MGM China, and variable-rate borrowings are about 12% of the total, so a 1 percentage point rate rise adds about USD 6.75 million of annual interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: liquidity, no maturity before 2027, scale across four segments, on-schedule refinancing record and falling capital expenditure. Weaknesses: earnings softening against fixed rent, off-debt commitments, Macau structure and discretionary shareholder returns. Opportunities that could lift credit quality: MGM Osaka opening on track for 2030, digital losses narrowing, Macau share gains and further disposals that cut rent. Threats: further room-rate or hold declines, MGM Osaka cost increases, the Macau concession expiry and a second landlord guarantee being confirmed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-07-29_mgmex991q22026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are Strong, because revenue was USD 17,537.683 million in FY2025 with a record Macau market share; competitive advantage is Average, because rates and hold move with the cycle; business diversification is Average to Strong across four segments; cost and capex flexibility is Average, limited by rent and lease capital expenditure minimums; margin stability is Weak to Average after the 3.12 percentage point fall in the Las Vegas segment margin; and free cash flow stability is Average, with 5.50% lower nine-month free cash flow. Ability to refinance is Strong given on-schedule refinancing and no maturity before 2027, liquidity is Strong at 2.15x cover of 2027 and 2028 maturities, and financial policy and governance is Average with Medium risk because buybacks and the voting agreement are discretionary. Main supports are liquidity and conduct, main constraints are rent, off-debt commitments and Macau structure, the trend is lower leverage on lower earnings, and the key missing datapoints are covenant levels, the voting agreement terms and any earnings guidance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C10; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are management's statements that October trading has rebounded and (in April) that convention bookings were solid, Macau share gains, narrowing digital losses and lower capital expenditure; the headwinds are lower Las Vegas rates, regional slot handle down 9% in Q3 2026, union contracts expiring in 2026, USD 360 million to USD 410 million of remaining 2026 capital expenditure and quarterly MGM Osaka funding. Over three to five years the opening of MGM Osaka, targeted for 2030, could add earnings but also adds uncapped completion guarantees, and the Macau concession expiry in 2032 and the lease commitments run alongside. Management comments are statements by the company, not evidence of results.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Initiating condition: Las Vegas room rates keep falling, as the 8% decline in Q3 2026 shows, and Macau hold returns toward the 25.0% of the prior-year nine months from 27.3%. First operating break: Las Vegas EBITDAR falls faster than revenue, as it did in Q3 2026 (11.66% against 1.53%), and the 2.30 percentage point hold reversion would remove about USD 145.94 million of Macau segment profit after gaming taxes over nine months. Financial transmission: adjusted EBITDA 10% lower would lift net leverage to 1.63x and cut fixed-charge cover to 1.61x. Liquidity, leverage and refinancing: cash and the undrawn revolver of USD 4,670.957 million still cover the USD 2,175.000 million due in 2027 and 2028 2.15x, but MGM China cash of USD 598 million covers its USD 750 million 2027 notes only 0.80x, so subsidiary refinancing or dividends matter. Management levers: cut the discretionary buyback (USD 1.4 billion authorised), slow MGM Osaka calls, sell Springfield (USD 443 million), and draw the revolver. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2028 on the sourced figures, and the observable triggers are rates, hold, revolver use and buyback pace. The scenario is mechanical, not a forecast, and does not assume default.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C10; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_mgmex991q32026earningrelea.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, MGM presents an adequate business profile supported by liquidity, scale across four segments and an on-schedule refinancing record, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that are softening against fixed rent, off-debt commitments and a Macau structure outside the guarantee group. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: nine-month operating cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 1,041.360 million, but it is fully allocated. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on stable adjusted EBITDA and on buybacks staying below free cash flow while MGM Osaka calls continue. The primary downside path is a further fall in Las Vegas pricing or Macau hold against fixed rent and MGM Osaka funding. Further analysis would require covenant levels, the voting agreement terms, a reconciliation of the landlord guarantees, earnings guidance and market data.
